title: Kartause Ittingen, Warth
meta: Quieter discovery | monastery, gardens and museums
body: A former Carthusian monastery with historic courtyards, gardens, a farm shop, the Ittinger Museum and Kunstmuseum Thurgau. Self-guided discovery routes explore its water, woodland and monastic history. The gardens are accessible in spring; the rose display belongs to a later season.
caption: Kartause Ittingen
familyNote: Choose short discovery walks and the grounds for an easy family visit; the museums suit children according to their interests.
aprilNote: The grounds are a spring option. Roses flower later; museum visits follow the standing winter opening hours.

title: Seebachtal lakes near Hüttwilen and Nussbaumen
meta: Quieter discovery | lakes, walking and nature
body: The Hüttwilersee, Nussbaumersee and Hasensee lie in a protected landscape of reeds, woodland and farmland. Lakeside walking and birdwatching are the main activities. This is one of the quieter natural settings close to Frauenfeld, with low-altitude paths suitable for spring conditions.
caption: Hüttwilersee in the Seebachtal
familyNote: Choose a short section of accessible route 918 with a pushchair, rather than committing to a full circuit of the lakes.
aprilNote: Low-altitude nature walks fit this visit. Individual natural paths can be muddy after rain; this is a walking outing rather than a swimming stop.

title: Altnau apple trail and orchard country
meta: Quieter discovery | orchards and a themed trail
body: The Altnau apple trail runs through orchards near Lake Constance, with themed information stations about fruit growing. The countryside and themed trail can be explored independently of the blossom.
caption: Apple blossom in Altnau, flowering is not guaranteed during this visit
familyNote: An easy orchard outing if the children enjoy themed walking trails. Choose the distance to suit the youngest.
aprilNote: The trail is accessible, but apple blossom is not dependable this early. Check the local blossom report before making a special journey.

title: Insel Werd, Eschenz
meta: Quieter discovery | island, chapel and footbridge
body: A small monastery island near Eschenz, connected to the shore by a wooden footbridge. The chapel and views across the water make it a short, quiet sight close to Stein am Rhein. The island also has prehistoric archaeological significance.
links: Thurgau Tourism on Werd and the region
caption: Footbridge to Insel Werd
familyNote: A short footbridge and island visit, best combined with nearby Stein am Rhein.
aprilNote: No summer attraction is needed for this short outdoor stop. Chapel services and any local access notices should be respected.

title: Rhine Falls / Rheinfall
meta: Waterfall, viewing platforms and boat trips
body: A wide waterfall below Schloss Laufen, with riverside viewpoints, platforms close to the water and boat trips. Viewpoints on the north bank provide an alternative to the stepped rock excursion.
caption: Rhine Falls and Schloss Laufen
familyNote: Use the riverside viewpoints or a short round trip without a rock landing. The Rock Experience has over 100 steps and is not recommended below 1.2 metres in height.
aprilNote: The falls can be viewed year-round. Boat operators normally serve the spring season, but their exact 2027 departures still need checking.

title: Schaffhausen old town and Munot fortress
meta: Old town and historic fortress
body: Schaffhausen has a historic old town with painted facades and projecting windows. The circular Munot fortress rises above the town and Rhine, surrounded by vineyards. The fortress adds ramparts, interior spaces and elevated views to the old-town sights.
caption: Munot fortress
familyNote: The old town is a flexible family stop. Munot adds steep approaches, stairs and a cobbled ramp, so it takes more effort with a pushchair.
aprilNote: The standing October-to-April Munot hours are 09:00 to 17:00. Combine the town with Rhine Falls rather than assuming summer events are running.

title: Stein am Rhein
meta: Medieval old town and riverfront
body: A compact medieval town where Lake Constance becomes the Rhine. Painted facades and decorated houses surround Rathausplatz, with riverfront scenery nearby. Its preserved centre is the main attraction; Insel Werd is a separate, quieter sight in neighbouring Eschenz.
caption: Painted houses in Stein am Rhein
familyNote: A compact old-town and riverfront stop. Pair it with Insel Werd if the children have energy for another short walk.
aprilNote: The outdoor town visit fits early April. Boat services and museum interiors are separate activities with their own opening arrangements.

title: Zurich old town, Lindenhof and the lake
meta: Old town, viewpoint and lakefront
body: Zurich's old town spreads along the Limmat, with lanes, churches and riverfront buildings. The elevated Lindenhof has views over the old town; the lakefront opens out toward Lake Zurich. Scheduled boat services add a separate activity on the water.
caption: Grossmünster and the Limmat
familyNote: Keep the old-town walk short and add the lakefront or a tram ride. Zurich Zoo offers a separate family outing nearby.
aprilNote: The city walk does not depend on a seasonal attraction. Check the selected boat service before including a lake cruise.

title: Technorama, Winterthur
meta: Interactive science centre | indoors and outdoors
body: A hands-on science centre in Winterthur with hundreds of experiments involving natural phenomena and technology. Visitors operate the exhibits themselves. Indoor galleries and an outdoor experiment park offer different ways to explore.
caption: An exhibit at Technorama
familyNote: A hands-on indoor option for mixed ages. The operator recommends The Sound of Wood for small children; children aged 0 to 5 currently enter free.
aprilNote: The standing schedule is daily, 10:00 to 17:00. Indoor exhibits make this a useful rainy-day choice; outdoor experiments depend on conditions.

title: Lucerne old town and lakefront
meta: Historic city, wooden bridge and lake
body: Lucerne's covered wooden Chapel Bridge crosses the Reuss beside the Water Tower. The old town has historic squares and painted buildings, while the lakefront looks across Lake Lucerne toward the mountains. Scheduled lake cruises are another activity from the city.
links: Chapel Bridge and its Water Tower
caption: Chapel Bridge, Lucerne
familyNote: A flexible old-town and lakefront visit with short walking sections. Combine it with a lake trip or the transport museum according to the children's energy.
aprilNote: The town sights fit early April. Lake cruises follow their spring timetable; mountain excursions need their own operating checks.

title: Swiss Museum of Transport / Verkehrshaus
meta: Interactive transport museum | indoors and outdoors
body: An interactive museum about transport and mobility, with trains, aircraft, road vehicles and shipping exhibits. It is open 365 days a year. The planetarium, cinema and Swiss Chocolate Adventure are additional attractions with separate ticket or package arrangements.
links: Plan a visit and compare tickets
caption: Swiss Museum of Transport
familyNote: The museum offers activities from age 2 and is the easiest all-weather family option here. The traffic garden and extra shows have separate age guidance; the Chocolate Adventure is recommended from age 6.
aprilNote: Open 365 days a year under the standing policy. Check the day's opening times and attraction programme. Museum entry and the additional attractions use different ticket arrangements.

title: Rigi by cogwheel train
meta: Mountain railway and viewpoints
body: Cogwheel railways reach Rigi's viewpoints above Lake Lucerne. The Vitznau route provides a lakeside approach to Rigi Kaltbad and Rigi Kulm. Railway access and mountain-path conditions are separate considerations.
caption: Rigi railway in snowy conditions
familyNote: The train provides mountain scenery without a long hike. Cold, remaining snow and transfers require planning with a three-year-old; use suitable short paths rather than assuming summer hiking access.
aprilNote: The published Vitznau-Rigi Kulm timetable covers all nine days. Goldau-Rigi Staffel is closed 5 to 23 April 2027. Weggis-Rigi Kaltbad is under maintenance through 2 April. Using Vitznau both ways avoids both closures; choose a clear forecast.

title: Unterseen and the Aare riverside
meta: Quieter discovery | old town and riverside
body: A historic town beside the Aare, near Interlaken West. Stadthausplatz, old buildings and the riverside are the main sights. Unterseen offers a quieter town setting close to central Interlaken.
caption: Unterseen and the Aare
familyNote: A short town and riverside outing that can be adjusted around the youngest child's energy. Useful while staying near Interlaken.
aprilNote: The town walk does not depend on summer openings. Choose a short riverside section suited to the day's conditions.

title: Spiez bay on Lake Thun
meta: Lakefront, harbour and castle
body: Spiez's bay on Lake Thun has a harbour, a castle park and church above the waterfront, with vineyards behind. The bay is an outdoor attraction in its own right, with boat connections to other Lake Thun destinations.
caption: Spiez Castle and Lake Thun
familyNote: The bay and castle park make a flexible outdoor stop. Allow for the hill between the railway station and the waterfront.
aprilNote: The castle museum, shop and cafe are closed until 1 May 2027. The park remains accessible; the church's standing winter hours are weekdays 10:00 to 17:00, subject to events. Lake Thun boats have a published spring 2027 timetable.

title: Brienz village and Lake Brienz
meta: Village, chalets and lake cruises
body: A lakeside village known for wooden chalets, woodcarving and its waterfront promenade. Brunngasse is one of its historic streets. A lake cruise adds views from the water.
caption: Lake Brienz, viewed from Oberried
familyNote: Choose the waterfront and village, with an optional boat ride. A train in one direction keeps the excursion shorter than a full boat round trip.
aprilNote: Lake Brienz boats run from 26 March 2027. The spring timetable has daily Interlaken Ost departures for Brienz at 10:10, 12:10 and 14:10, returning from Brienz at 11:10, 13:10 and 15:10. Summer steamers are a separate later-season offering.

title: Ringgenberg and a short lakeside walk
meta: Quieter discovery | lakeside village and castle-church
body: Ringgenberg stands on Lake Brienz's north shore, with a castle-church above the lake and paths through woodland and along the shore. Nearby Goldswil and Burgseeli add a smaller lake setting.
caption: Ringgenberg castle-church
familyNote: Choose a short village or lakeside section; longer wooded paths and slopes need more planning with a pushchair.
aprilNote: Spring 2027 boats do not call at Ringgenberg, so arrive by land. Burgseeli lido is a summer activity, not an April swimming option.

title: Giessbach Falls
meta: Waterfalls, woodland and historic hotel
body: The Giessbach descends through woodland in 14 cascades toward Lake Brienz, beside the historic Grandhotel Giessbach. Paths connect viewpoints around the falls, and a funicular links the lakeside landing with the hotel.
caption: Giessbach Falls
familyNote: Sloping waterfall paths can be wet and slippery. A carrier is more practical than relying on a pushchair for the falls; funicular pushchair capacity is limited.
aprilNote: The published spring boat timetable includes Giessbach calls, but the funicular's exact 2027 dates are not yet verified here. Confirm the funicular and path conditions before travelling.

title: Lauterbrunnen valley and Staubbach views
meta: Cliff scenery, waterfalls and valley walks
body: A valley of high cliffs, meadows and waterfalls, including Staubbach Falls beside Lauterbrunnen village. Valley-floor paths provide views of the cliffs and falling water.
caption: Lauterbrunnen valley from Wengen
familyNote: Use a short valley-floor walk for the cliff and waterfall views. Combine it with the train to Wengen if the family wants a longer outing.
aprilNote: Staubbach Falls can be viewed year-round. The gallery behind the waterfall opens May to October and is not part of this April plan. Check valley-path conditions after snow or bad weather.

title: Wengen by train from Lauterbrunnen
meta: Mountain village and railway ride
body: A largely car-free mountain village above Lauterbrunnen, reached by the Wengernalp Railway. The village has traditional chalet architecture and views across the valley.
caption: Wengen village
familyNote: The railway ride and village suit a family outing. Remaining snow, hills and chilly weather make short village walks easier than higher routes.
aprilNote: The village railway is a year-round connection. Recheck the travel-day timetable and operating notices; summer hiking routes and mountain lifts have separate seasons.

title: Harder Kulm above Interlaken
meta: Mountain viewpoint and funicular
body: A funicular from Interlaken reaches this viewpoint above the town, with views over Lakes Thun and Brienz. It offers a short mountain excursion when the railway is operating.
caption: Harder Kulm and Lake Thun
familyNote: A short funicular ride and viewpoint outing when operating. The viewing platform and short approach suit a brief visit; longer mountain paths need a separate conditions check.
aprilNote: An official opening date covering 1 to 9 April 2027 could not be verified. Keep this available as an option, but confirm the operator's season before planning around it.

title: Trümmelbach Falls
meta: Waterfalls inside a mountain
body: Ten glacial waterfalls inside the mountain, reached through a system of tunnels, a lift and stairs. The water drains the glacier walls of the Eiger, Moench and Jungfrau.
caption: Trümmelbach Falls
familyNote: The operator does not admit a three-year-old. Older family members could visit separately; tunnels, stairs, noise and wet surfaces add difficulty.
aprilNote: The usual season begins in early April, subject to weather. Confirm the actual 2027 opening before travelling; an open date does not remove the child-access restriction.

title: Aare Gorge / Aareschlucht, Meiringen
meta: Gorge walk and tunnels
body: Walkways and tunnels follow the Aare through a narrow limestone gorge. The Tatzi trail adds a creature-search activity.
links: 2027 dates, Tatzi trail and pushchair information
caption: Aare Gorge
familyNote: Narrow, light pushchairs can reach the main attractions from the west entrance, subject to crowd restrictions. Plan an out-and-back visit rather than a full through-walk.
aprilNote: Confirmed 2027 dates: west entrance opens 26 March; east entrance opens 6 May. During this visit the published opening hours are 08:30 to 17:30, with return via the west entrance.

title: Natur- und Tierpark Goldau
meta: Wildlife park, woodland and family activities
body: A wildlife park in the wooded landscape of the Goldau landslide, home to native and European animal species. Some deer and other animals move through free-ranging areas, alongside larger animal enclosures.
familyNote: Animals and playgrounds make a flexible family day. Choose the main routes with a pushchair; some paths are less accessible. This is an alternative wildlife day to Zurich Zoo.
aprilNote: The standing April-to-October opening hours are daily, 09:00 to 18:00. This outing does not depend on the mountain railways operating; check the day's park notices before travelling.
caption: Visitors at the bear and wolf enclosure in Goldau

title: Thun old town, Schadau Park and castle
meta: Old town, lakefront park and an optional castle visit
body: Thun's old town sits beside the Aare below its medieval castle. Schadau Park adds an open lakeside setting at the outlet of Lake Thun. The castle museum provides views across the town, lake and mountains.
familyNote: The town and park can be explored in short sections. The castle interior has many stairs and no internal lift, so make that part optional for the youngest and leave the pushchair outside the museum.
aprilNote: The castle's standing April-to-June schedule is daily, 10:00 to 17:00, with last entry 30 minutes before closing. Unlike Spiez's museum, this is an April castle option; recheck any special closures.
links: Castle hours, stairs and family access
caption: Thun old town and castle

title: Zurich Zoo and Masoala Rainforest
meta: Zoo, animal habitats and indoor rainforest
body: Zurich Zoo combines outdoor animal habitats with the indoor Masoala Rainforest. A separate zoo visit adds an animal-focused outing to Zurich's old-town and lakefront sights.
familyNote: Choose a few animal areas rather than trying to cover the whole zoo with a three-year-old. Masoala provides an indoor part of the visit; outdoor sections still involve walking. Choose this or Goldau according to your route.
aprilNote: The zoo's standing policy is open 365 days a year. March-to-October hours are 09:00 to 18:00, with Masoala opening at 10:00. Recheck the travel-day notices and individual animal-area access.
caption: Inside the Masoala Rainforest at Zurich Zoo
